title: Pride of Oklahoma History: OU's Band Since 1904 and Its Sudler Trophy
question: When was the Pride of Oklahoma marching band founded and has it won the Sudler Trophy?
answer: The Pride of Oklahoma traces to 1904, when freshman Lloyd Curtis founded OU's first continuous student band. The band received the Sudler Trophy, one of college marching band's most prestigious national honors, in 1987.
summary: The Pride of Oklahoma dates to 1904, when Lloyd Curtis started OU's first continuous student band. It won the Sudler Trophy in 1987. Here is its history.
body: The Pride of Oklahoma is older than Memorial Stadium, older than the Schooner and older than statehood itself. Its roots go back to 1901, when Professor John Merrill put together a band made up mostly of townspeople that broke up after each football season. The lasting version arrived in 1904, when freshman Lloyd Curtis founded OU's first continuous student band.

It started as a pep band rather than a military drill unit, and it grew alongside the athletic program. In 1929 OU hired William R. Wehrend as its first full-time faculty member devoted mainly to the band, and in 1934 he became one of the first directors to admit women. That same year the band pulled off a famous publicity stunt, a drum roll that lasted ten hours.

National recognition followed. The band won the grand prize as best overall unit in the 1961 National Cherry Blossom Festival Parade in Washington. In 1987 the John Philip Sousa Foundation awarded it the Sudler Trophy, one of the most prestigious honors in college marching band, placing Oklahoma between Texas in 1986 and Michigan State in 1988 on the list of winners.

The modern Pride is around 300 members strong, and about three quarters of them major in something other than music. Its pregame show, introduced under longtime director Gene Thrailkill, has been used in some form for decades. In 2007 the Pride made its first trip to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York.
